deepDive.title: Anthropic Plants 10 AI Agents at JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, and Citi
deepDive.html:
Overview

Anthropic just made its most aggressive push into financial services yet. At a New York event on May 5, CEO Dario Amodei shared the stage with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon to announce 10 purpose-built AI agents for banks and insurers — already running in production at JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citi, AIG, and Visa. Fortune has the full story.

The Details

  • 10 specialized agents covering pitchbook building, earnings review, financial statement auditing, credit memo drafting, and KYC checks
  • Already live in production at JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citi, AIG, and Visa
  • Claude now integrates natively with Microsoft 365 — the dominant productivity suite across major financial firms
  • New data partnerships with Moody's and Dun & Bradstreet give Claude direct access to credit ratings and business intelligence feeds
  • Simultaneous announcement: a $1.5B joint venture with Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs to build an AI-native enterprise services firm

Why It Matters

This isn't a vague partnership press release. Anthropic has specific, named workflows running in production at the most scrutinized financial institutions on earth. When JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs standardize on the same AI infrastructure, it creates an industry default — and applies direct pressure to every mid-size bank still circling the vendor shortlist.

The Microsoft 365 integration and Moody's data access are the real unlock. They eliminate the two biggest deployment friction points: document workflows and data connectivity. Banks still in pilot mode risk being a full generation behind by the time regulators publish their AI governance framework.

items.tagline: Enterprise AI agents for customer service, insurance claims, and mortgage refinancing
items.summary: Sierra raised $950M at a $15B valuation this week, led by Tiger Global and GV. Founded by ex-Salesforce CEO Bret Taylor, its agents handle mortgage refinancing, insurance claims, and customer interactions at 40%+ of Fortune 50 companies, with $150M+ ARR two years post-launch.
items.analysis: **Why banks should care:** Sierra's agents run in production financial workflows at institutional scale — evidence that agentic AI in customer-facing finance has crossed from experimental to proven.

items.tagline: Agentic AI platform that charges clients only on measurable efficiency improvements
items.summary: Trase emerged from stealth with a $10.5M pre-seed led by Red Cell Partners. Co-founded by Grant Verstandig, the McLean startup embeds engineers inside client orgs to build AI workflows — currently serving healthcare and national security, including an active U.S. Navy contract.
items.analysis: **The pricing model matters:** Trase charges only on proven efficiency gains — directly addressing the ROI barrier that stalls agentic AI adoption in compliance-heavy financial institutions.

items.headline: Fed Exempts Agentic AI from Model Risk Rules in Landmark Regulatory Shift
items.summary: Fed Vice Chair Bowman announced May 1 that revised MRM guidance explicitly excludes generative and agentic AI — removing the SR 11-7 validation burden that has slowed bank deployments. The guidance now applies narrowly to traditional models only, signaling regulators are choosing innovation over obstruction.
items.keyPoint: **Compliance unlock for banks.** Agentic AI deployments no longer require full model risk governance overhead — removing the biggest internal barrier to production rollouts at regulated institutions.

items.headline: GPT-5.5 Instant Is Now ChatGPT's Default Model — With 52% Fewer Finance and Law Hallucinations
items.summary: OpenAI rolled GPT-5.5 Instant to all ChatGPT users on May 5, replacing GPT-5.3. Internal tests show 52.5% fewer hallucinations on high-stakes finance, law, and medicine prompts. Cross-session memory now draws from past conversations, connected files, and Gmail.
items.keyPoint: **Better accuracy, new governance questions.** Enterprise ChatGPT users get improved financial-document accuracy automatically — but persistent cross-session memory creates fresh data confidentiality requirements for bank deployments.

items.headline: Google Silently Ships Gemini 3.2 Flash at $0.25/M Tokens Ahead of I/O
items.summary: Gemini 3.2 Flash appeared quietly in Google AI Studio and the iOS app on May 5 — no press release, priced at $0.25/M input tokens. Early benchmarks suggest near-Gemini 3.1 Pro performance on coding and reasoning. A formal reveal is expected at Google I/O on May 19-20.
items.keyPoint: **Cheapest frontier-class model yet.** At $0.25/M tokens, Gemini 3.2 Flash makes high-volume document automation economically viable for institutions that couldn't justify frontier API costs before.

items.headline: Bank AI Survey: 91% Call It Strategic. Only 23% Are Past the Pilot Stage.
items.summary: Accenture's Q1 2026 banking survey found 91% of executives call AI a strategic priority — but only 23% have moved beyond pilots into production. Fraud detection leads as the most mature application; KYC and compliance automation lag despite now-reduced regulatory barriers.
items.keyPoint: **The deployment gap is widening.** Tier-one banks are in production while most mid-size institutions are still piloting. With the regulatory friction now cleared, there's no longer a credible excuse to wait.

items.headline: OpenAI Grants EU Pre-Launch Access to Cyber AI Model as Government Scrutiny of Frontier Models Grows
items.summary: OpenAI agreed to give EU regulators early access to GPT-5.5-Cyber ahead of public release. Microsoft and xAI made similar concessions. Anthropic's 'Mythos' model — capable of identifying vulnerabilities in legacy systems — remains withheld and is drawing regulatory scrutiny.
items.keyPoint: **Government oversight is accelerating.** Banks using AI for cybersecurity and fraud detection should expect stricter model documentation requirements as regulators gain direct evaluation access to frontier AI.
